Rashi on Sotah 46b:10:1.english: They compel [one] for accompaniment - They compel one who does not want to accompany his fellow on the road to accompany him.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:11:1.hebrew: ויקרא שמה לוז - סיפיה דקרא "היא שמה עד היום הזה", ומיניה יליף דלא נתבלבלה ולא חרבה, כדאמרינן: כל מקום שנאמר "עד היום הזה", לעולם ולעולמי עולמים הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:11:1.english: And he called its name Luz - The end of the verse [is] "that is its name to this day," and from it [the baraita] derives that it was not disarranged and was not destroyed, as we say: Wherever it is stated "to this day," it is forever and for all eternity.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:12:1.english: And for his descendants - As we say, that the Angel of Death has no dominion over them.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:12:2.hebrew: שלא דבר בפיו - דלא כתיב אלא "ויראם" — באצבעו או בעקמימות שפתים — כדלקמן:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:12:2.english: Who did not speak with his mouth - For it is only written, "and he showed them" — with his finger or with a curving of [his] lips — as [stated] below.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:14:1.english: That Pharaoh accompanied him - As it is written: “And Pharaoh gave men charge concerning him, and they sent him away.”

Rashi on Sotah 46b:14:2.english: He is not harmed - [That is,] the one who sets out on a journey.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:15:1.hebrew: עד עיבורה של עיר - שהוא יוצא ממנה, והוא בבית החיצון שבתוך שבעים אמה ושירים לבתי העיר:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:15:1.english: Until the outskirts of the city - When he [the student] leaves it, and he is at the outermost house that is within seventy cubits and a fraction of the houses of the city.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:16:1.hebrew: בי ציניתא דבבל - מקום הוא ובו דקלים הרבה, כמו ציני הר הברזל (סוכה דף כט:):
Rashi on Sotah 46b:16:1.english: Bei Tzinyata of Babylonia - It is a place, and in it are many palm trees, like "the palm trees [tzinei] of the Iron Mountain" (Sukkah 29b).

Rashi on Sotah 46b:17:1.hebrew: לא נתיישב - והיינו ״לא ישב אדם שם״: לא גזר אדם הראשון יישוב שם. והיינו דאמרי אינשי ״איתנהו משני אדם הראשון״ — שגזר עליו אדם הראשון יישוב דקלים ולא יישוב אחר:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:17:1.english: Was not settled - And this is [the meaning of] "no man [adam] dwelt there": Adam the first man did not decree settlement there. And this is [the meaning of] what people say, "they have existed since the years of Adam the first man" — for Adam the first man decreed upon it [that place] a settlement of date palms, and not any other settlement.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:1:1.english: Firm [eitan] is your dwelling-place, and your nest is set in the rock - Thus, eitan is a rock.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:1:2.hebrew: מוסדי ארץ - הם הרים, וכל הר של אבנים הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:1:2.english: The foundations of the earth - They are mountains, and every mountain is [made] of stones.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:1:3.english: That it is old - And not that its ground was brought anew from another land.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:1:4.english: A nation from of old - That is, old.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:20:1.hebrew: שהקרחת עלינו את המקום - שכשהיו המים הרעים, היתה פרנסתינו להביא מים ולמכור:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:20:1.english: For you have made the place bald for us - For when the waters were bad, our livelihood was to bring water and sell [it].

Rashi on Sotah 46b:20:2.english: Of little faith - For they were worried that their livelihood had ceased because the waters were healed.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:21:1.hebrew: ודלמא - קטנים ממש הוו, ועל שם מקומם נקראו נערים, שהיו מן נעורן:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:21:1.english: And perhaps - They were actually little [children], and they were called ne’arim after their place [of origin], as they were from Ne’oran.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:21:2.english: Here their place is specified - Jericho.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:2:1.english: From a bird sin-offering - For it is written regarding it: "from opposite the back of its neck" (Leviticus 5[:8]).

Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:1.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי - דהא כתיב ולא יזרע, משמע להבא, מדלא כתיב ואשר לא יזרע, דלהוי משמע לשעבר:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:1.english: No one disagrees - For it is written “and it shall not be sown,” [which] implies the future, since it is not written “and which was not sown,” which would imply the past.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:2.hebrew: מי כתיב ולא יעבד - אי הוה כתיב אל נחל איתן ולא יעבד בו, הוה משמע להבא. אבל השתא דכתיב לא יעבד, משמע לשעבר, דאשר לאו לשון צואה הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:2.english: Does it state: “And shall not be worked” - If it were written, “to a rough valley, and it shall not be worked in it,” it would imply the future. But now that it is written, “[which] is not worked,” it implies the past, for “which” is not an expression of command.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:3.hebrew: אשר לשעבר משמע - אע"ג דלא יעבד להבא משמע, הני מילי בלאו אשר, אבל השתא דכתיב אשר, על כרחיך מוכח עלה דלשעבר הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:3.english: [The term] "which" indicates the past - Even though "will not be worked" indicates the future, that applies without [the word] "which"; but now that "which" is written, it perforce proves regarding it that it [refers] to the past.

Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:4.hebrew: רבויא הוא - לא בא אלא לרבות כל עבודות כדלקמן, דלא תדרשיה בכלל ופרט:
Rashi on Sotah 46b:4:4.english: It is an amplification - It only comes to include all [forms of] labor, as [explained] below, so that you should not expound it as a generalization and specification.
